_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); electric utility signals

pit_profile.why: The Southern Company: 'The traditional electric operating companies – Alabama Power, Georgia Power, and Mississippi Power – are each operating public utility companies providing electric service to retail customers in three Southeastern states in addition to wholesale customers in the Southeast. Southern Company Gas is an energy services holding company whose primary business is the distribution of natural gas in four states – Illinois, Georgia, Virginia, and Tennessee – through the natural gas distribution utilities.'; among its risk factors, 'Southern Company and its subsidiaries are subject to substantial federal, state, and local governmental regulation, including with respect to rates.', 'The operating results of the Registrants are affected by weather conditions and may fluctuate on a seasonal basis.' and 'The Southern Company system's costs of compliance with environmental laws and satisfying related AROs are significant.' (its own FY2021 10-K); ENERGY_TRANSITION is live (from 2015-12-12) but out of scope: Southern Company's own FY2021 10-K no longer says it owns coal reserves for its plants, and the one mine it names ('Mississippi Power owns a lignite mine that was intended to provide fuel for the Kemper IGCC.') served the abandoned Kemper IGCC ('As a result of the abandonment of the Kemper IGCC, final mine reclamation began in 2018 and was substantially completed in 2020, with monitoring expected to continue through 2028.'), so it holds no reserves for decarbonisation to strand; no other live theme's scope names what an electric utility sells, so the watch list is empty and its risk factor 'The Southern Company system may be exposed to regulatory and financial risks related to the impact of GHG legislation, regulation, and emission reduction goals.' stays here (the PEP obesity rule)

BEAR.desc: EPS -34.9%/yr (worst year FY12-FY21 ex-FY17, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +10.6%/yr (Q4 revenue + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr ex-FY17 median

BULL.desc: EPS +10.6%/yr (FY12-FY21 ex-FY17 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +16.2%/yr (best 2-yr run FY12-FY21 ex-FY17); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: SO (retrospective, 2022-03-11) ✕ AVOID — Ratio B 2.35x (69.4% downside to Bear $21 / +29.6% upside to Bull $89) | Adj composite 1.81 vs market 2.91: gap -1.10 [OVERVALUED] | +29% above the EPP floor $53 (15x FY22E $3.55) | Conservative 2-yr case: +11.5% total (+5.7%/yr) | At 19.3x FY22E the 15% hurdle price $91 sits above the BULL case; retail kWh sales -0.6% in Q4 2021, forward revenues +12.7% (no Q1 2022 revenue guide, Q4 2021 revenue as reported); ENERGY_TRANSITION is live but out of scope: the 10-K names no coal reserves for the company's plants.
